name: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
watch: Eight artists altered their works on 15 February 2024 and demanded removal of board members and funders. Galleries closed a month.
why_flagged: No donor roster published. FY2025 revenue $9.3M, expenses $11.6M. The 2021 artist income pilot ran with the SF Arts Commission and Grants for the Arts.
records_note: It posts annual reports from 2004 to 2024, audited statements and Form 990s back to 2008, a donor list for fiscal 2024 and nine directors.

name: Smithsonian, Air and Space
watch: Boeing, Northrop Grumman and Lockheed name galleries; Koch hall kept.
why_flagged: Boeing, Northrop Grumman and Lockheed name galleries; Koch hall kept.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2016 to 2025, a named donor page and a board; the Smithsonian posts audited accounts for 2017 to 2025.

name: DK Rozy (Rosa's House of Culture)
watch: Dedicated to working-class education, feminist theory, and anti-war solidarity.

name: Typography Center for Contemporary Art
watch: Autonomous contemporary art center founded in 2012 by artist group ZIP. Served as southern Russia's primary independent artistic laboratory and KICA school.

name: GES-2 House of Culture
funding: Funded through the V-A-C Foundation, endowed by Leonid Mikhelson, CEO and key shareholder of Novatek, Russia's major natural gas producer.
watch: Opened Dec 2021 as Russia's largest private art centre. Artistic director Francesco Manacorda resigned Mar 2022. In 2023 Ural Biennial founder Alisa Prudnikova became its director. GES-2 also appears as a sponsor on the Tretyakov Gallery's 2026 partner list.
why_flagged: Opened Dec 2021 as Russia's largest private art centre. Artistic director Francesco Manacorda resigned Mar 2022. In 2023 Ural Biennial founder Alisa Prudnikova became its director. GES-2 also appears as a sponsor on the Tretyakov Gallery's 2026 partner list.
records_note: GES-2 posts no annual report, accounts, donor or sponsor list, or board; the site names only the founder Leonid Mikhelson.

name: The State Hermitage Museum
funding: Federal budget of the Russian Federation and state corporate sponsorships (VTB Bank, Gazprom).
watch: Director Mikhail Piotrovsky explicitly weaponized museum diplomacy as 'cultural operations' in support of state military aggression; federal state ideological alignment.

name: The State Tretyakov Gallery
funding: Federal Ministry of Culture budget, state-controlled banking sponsors.
watch: Director Zelfira Tregulova removed 9 Feb 2023 after a Ministry-forwarded complaint of 'destructive ideology' in the displays; Elena Pronicheva (daughter of an FSB general) replaced her; in Jan 2026 Olga Galaktionova (ex-ROSIZO, ex-Pushkin) took over. The Ministry cancelled the 9th Moscow Biennale at the New Tretyakov on 3 Nov 2022. The Gallery states 80+ companies and individuals support it.
why_flagged: Corporate partners include VTB, Sberbank, PSB, Gazprombank, Transneft, LUKOIL, Surgutneftegas and NOVATEK. Private patrons include Leonid Mikhelson and Alisher Usmanov; the V. Potanin Foundation also gives.
records_note: The gallery posts annual reports (2015 to 2020 seen), fund reports to 2025, a named trustees list and a named thanks list for corporate supporters.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, 2009-06: Embassy Moscow followed the criminal trial of former Tretyakov curator Andrei Yerofeyev over the 2007 Forbidden Art show. (Cablegate 09MOSCOW1688)

name: Ў Gallery of Contemporary Art
records_note: Closed on 29 October 2020; its domain now shows only a default web-server page, with no reports, accounts, funders or board.

name: National Art Museum of the Republic of Belarus
funding: Direct state budget of the Republic of Belarus under the presidential administration.
watch: State museum founded 1939, 30,000+ objects, Lenina 20. Its 'Exhibition of One Masterpiece: Marc Chagall, A Stroll' (8 Apr–21 Sep 2026) is lent by the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg, and sponsored by Sber Bank (Belarus); the museum ran a Belgazprombank 'Autumn Salon' partnership in the 2010s. Attendance is not published on the pages opened; budget is far below US$15M, so S.

name: Sun Mu Studio & North Korean Dissident Art Archive
watch: Independent studio and archive established by pseudonymous North Korean defector artist Sun Mu ('No Line / Border'). Dedicated to subversive critiques of Kim dynasty totalitarianism and preserving defector experiences.

name: Mansudae Art Studio
funding: Directly financed by the Workers' Party of Korea and state treasury, augmented by overseas monument export revenues.
watch: Founded 17 Nov 1959; c.4,000 staff incl. c.700–1,000 artists; 120,000 m² complex. Exhibitions abroad: London 2007 and 2014, Brisbane 2009, Dandong 2013, Beijing 798 gallery from 2009. Kotra estimates North Korea earned over US$160m from art sales in the decade to 2018. Koryo Tours' guide says the studio 'is on the UN sanction list and cannot be visited nor art purchased'.

name: Korean Art Gallery
funding: Workers' Party of Korea state budget.
watch: The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: National fine-art museum with 22 display rooms; KCNA claimed 6 million cumulative visitors by 2020. Budget unpublished.
records_note: Its listed address, korart.sca.kp, does not resolve from outside North Korea, so no records could be checked.
